question: Let \[N=123456789101112\dots4344\] be the \(79\)-digit number that is formed by writing the integers from \(1\) to \(44\) in order, one after the other. What is the remainder when \(N\) is divided by \(45?\)
solution:
Because \(45=5\cdot9\), the last digit and the digit sum provide useful divisibility information.

To count the digit sum, temporarily include the integer \(0\), which contributes nothing. In the four blocks \(0\) through \(9\), \(10\) through \(19\), \(20\) through \(29\), and \(30\) through \(39\), the units digits contribute four copies of \(0+1+\cdots+9\). The tens digits contribute ten copies each of \(1,2,3\). Finally, \(40\) through \(44\) contribute five tens digits equal to \(4\), along with units digits \(0,1,2,3,4\). Thus the digit sum is
\[
4(0+1+\cdots+9)+10(1+2+3)+5\cdot4+(0+1+2+3+4)
=180+60+20+10=270.
\]
Since \(270=9\cdot30\), the digit-sum rule shows that \(N\) is divisible by \(9\). Therefore \(N-9\) is also divisible by \(9\).

The last two digits of \(N\) are \(44\), so \(N-9\) ends in \(35\) and is divisible by \(5\). Since \(5\) and \(9\) are relatively prime, \(N-9\) is divisible by \(45\). As \(0\le9<45\), the remainder is \(\boxed{9}\), choice \(\text{C}\).
